title: Spectral sequences and convergence
summary: The common language of convergence for spectral sequences in an arbitrary abelian category, on Mathlib's SpectralSequence carrier and Tau Ceti's spectral-object abutments: cycle and boundary towers, stabilisation and the limit page; bidegree assignments, boundedness and Euler characteristics; weak, ordinary and strong convergence in a set of total degrees, morphisms, the comparison theorem and the standard consequences; the towers, limit page and convergence of spectral sequences of spectral objects (Stacks 24.13 in spectral-object form, Mathlib's quadrant cases); filtered complexes in classical indexing (finite, cohomologically bounded, exhaustive bounded below); exact couples in Mathlib's carrier and their identification with spectral objects; lim and lim¹ in abelian categories, Boardman's conditional convergence with the whole-plane obstruction, and the complete convergence theorem.

targets.name: CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.StabilizesAt
targets.statement: E stabilises at pq from page s if for all r ≥ s the page-r differentials leaving and entering pq vanish; E is regular (coregular) at pq if the leaving (entering) differentials vanish for all large r; E degenerates at s if all differentials of pages r ≥ s vanish. Regular iff Z_r(pq) eventually constant; coregular iff B_r(pq) eventually constant; stabilisation gives canonical isomorphisms (E.page s).X pq ≅ (E.page r).X pq for r ≥ s, compatible with composition and natural; degeneration at s implies stabilisation everywhere from s.

api.name: isRegularAt_iff

api.name: isCoregularAt_iff
api.statement: Coregular at pq iff B_r(pq) is eventually constant.

api.name: stableIso
api.statement: Canonical isomorphisms (E.page s).X pq ≅ (E.page r).X pq for r ≥ s, transitive and natural in morphisms.

api.name: stabilizesAt_of_degenerates

api.name: stabilizesAt_mono

targets.name: CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.IsBoundedBelow
targets.statement: With respect to a bidegree assignment: bounded below (∀ n ∃ β(n), E_{r₀}(pq) = 0 if deg pq = n, fil pq ≥ β(n)), bounded above (∃ α(n), vanishing if fil pq ≤ α(n)), bounded (both). Vanishing persists to later pages; bounded below ⇒ regular everywhere; bounded above ⇒ coregular everywhere; bounded ⇒ each pq of total degree n stabilises from the first r ≥ r₀ with r ≥ β(n+1) − fil pq + e and r ≥ fil pq − α(n−1) + e.

Finiteness in degree n alone does not suffice (1.4's filtered complex, n = 0).

targets.name: CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.eulerChar_page_succ
targets.statement: Let P contain zero and be closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects and under extensions, and v : C → G additive on short exact sequences with terms in P. If page r has finitely many nonzero positions, all in P, then so does page r+1 and Σ (−1)^{deg pq} v(E_r(pq)) = Σ (−1)^{deg pq} v(E_{r+1}(pq)). The cohomological page shapes carry the ComplexShape.EulerCharSigns instance (p,q) ↦ (−1)^{p+q}.
hypotheses: P weak Serre class (explicit closure hypotheses)
v additive on short exact sequences in P
finitely many nonzero positions on page r, all in P

targets.name: CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.fiveTerm_exact
targets.statement: For an E₂ cohomological spectral sequence with the standard assignment: (vanishing) convergence in degree n and E_r^{p,n−p} = 0 ∀p ⇒ H^n = 0; (dimension) over a field with finite dimensions, finitely many nonzero, finite filtration: dim H^n = Σ_p dim E_∞^{p,n−p} ≤ Σ_p dim E_r^{p,n−p}, with equality iff all differentials of pages r′ ≥ r leaving or entering total degree n vanish; (two columns) E_2^{p,q} = 0 for p ∉ {0,1} ⇒ 0 → E_2^{1,n−1} → H^n → E_2^{0,n} → 0; (two rows) E_2^{p,q} = 0 for q ∉ {0,1}, convergence in n, n+1 ⇒ E_2^{n−1,1} → E_2^{n+1,0} → H^{n+1} → E_2^{n,1} → E_2^{n+2,0} exact; (first quadrant) edge morphisms E_2^{n,0} ↠ F^nH^n ↪ H^n ↠ E_∞^{0,n} ↪ E_2^{0,n}, five-term sequence 0 → E_2^{1,0} → H^1 → E_2^{0,1} → E_2^{2,0} → H^2 under convergence in degrees 1, 2, and for m ≥ 1 with E_2^{p,q} = 0 for 0 < q < m: E_2^{j,0} ≅ H^j for j < m and 0 → E_2^{m,0} → H^m → E_2^{0,m} → E_2^{m+1,0} → H^{m+1}.
